2609.07255.title: SkillAlign: Aligning Skill Interfaces for LLM-based Agents
2609.07255.paper_summary: Language-model agents increasingly rely on skills: reusable procedural knowledge for reasoning, tool use, and interaction. Existing work studies how skills are acquired, retrieved, compressed, or composed, but often assumes that once a skill is selected, its interface to the agent is fixed. We argue that this overlooks a key source of skill utility: the same skill can help, distract, or mislead depending on how it is exposed. We propose SkillAlign, a provider-agnostic framework that represents candidate skills as multi-view procedural cards and renders them through alternative exposure interfaces, including full instructions, hints, compressed summaries, workflows, or no exposure. This enables counterfactual evaluation where the task, agent, and candidate skills are fixed while only the exposure interface varies. Across ALFWorld and SkillsBench, we show that exposure form substantially affects task success and rendered context cost, and that compact top-k exposure can outperform full-library injection. We further conduct a replay-based policy-learning analysis on ALFWorld, showing that adaptive exposure contains learnable signal but remains far from oracle selection. Our results suggest that skill-augmented agents should optimize not only which skills to use, but also how those skills are presented.
2609.07255.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型代理越來越依賴技能：可重用的程序性知識，用於推理、工具使用和互動。現有的研究探討了技能是如何獲得、檢索、壓縮或組合的，但通常假設一旦選擇了一項技能，其與代理的介面就是固定的。我們認為這忽略了一個關鍵的技能效用來源：同一技能可以根據其暴露方式而幫助、分心或誤導。我們提出了SkillAlign，一個供應商無關的框架，將候選技能表示為多視角的程序卡片，並通過替代的暴露介面進行呈現，包括完整的指示、提示、壓縮摘要、工作流程或不進行暴露。這使得反事實評估成為可能，其中任務、代理和候選技能是固定的，而只有暴露介面變化。在ALFWorld和SkillsBench中，我們顯示暴露形式對任務成功和呈現上下文成本有顯著影響，且緊湊的前k名暴露可以超越完整庫的注入。我們進一步在ALFWorld上進行了基於重播的政策學習分析，顯示自適應暴露包含可學習的信號，但仍然遠未達到最佳選擇。我們的結果表明，增強技能的代理不僅應優化使用哪些技能，還應優化這些技能的呈現方式。
